[中文](#cn-v0.2.0) | [English](#en-v0.2.0)

承接 `v0.1.0`。这一版把模拟器**接到真机上**，并把**浏览器试玩页**搬进仓库：
`op=handover` 去脚本源码里抽交接值（不让人抄 9 位数）、`op=bind` 一条命令把真机那份工程搭进模拟器、
`GET /miliastra/play` 是一页 PixiJS（WebGL）**真能玩**的试玩页（与面板、与 AI **共用同一个会话**）、
`op=cases` 把「这一版怎么验收」写成人机共读的一份清单。另修掉三次「画面为什么这么小」的根因
（最隐蔽的一次：footer 抢走了 217px）。

<h3 id="cn-v0.2.0">新增功能</h3>

- **★ 浏览器试玩页 `GET /miliastra/play`**：PixiJS（WebGL）真能玩的一页 —— 工具栏（开始 / 暂停 / 单步 / 重开 / 结束）+
  侧栏（状态 / 服务端变量 / 脚本 `print` / **这一局的操作时间线**）。它和面板、和 AI 走**同一个会话、同一份工程**，
  页面每 33ms 轮询增量场景，所以 **AI 一动，人那边的画面立刻跟着变**。页面靠 `attach()` 先接已有会话，接不上才新开一局
  —— 不会把人/AI 正在跑的局顶掉。
- **★ `op=handover`：交接值体检（别靠人抄）**：列出这台机器上的活文件（标出"当前正在开发"的那张图），
  再读那份 Lua，把源码里 `local NAME = <9 位以上整数>` 的**候选交接值**摆出来（含变量名与类型提示）+ 一份建议模板清单。
  为什么值得单开一步：**交接值抄错一位 → 脚本静默什么都不建**（不报错、日志无痕），抽真值比让人抄一遍可靠。
- **★ `op=bind`：一条命令把真机工程搬进模拟器**：给 `source`（活文件路径）+ `templates:[{guid,kind}]`（**创作者交接的模板索引**）
  + `containerId` 即可。默认顺手起一次会话，回「脚本跑没跑（`run.logs`）」与「控件建了几个（`run.controlCount`）」；
  成功一次会**记一份配方**，之后 `{"op":"bind","last":true}` 一键重搭。
- **★ `op=cases`：验收单（人 / AI 读同一份）**：把「这一版怎么验收」存成一条条用例 —— 自动项**确定性重放**，
  **人工项只列出、不代跑也不代判**。回执直说「自动项已跑完 —— 但整组没算过：还有 N 条人工项」。
- **`op=verify` 支持 `fromHistory:true`：人在试玩页里刚玩的**那一局**，直接变成回归用例** —— AI 不用手抄事件序列。
- **`op=verify` 支持拖拽与数量断言**：`drag:{from,to,steps?,gap?}` 自动展开成 `down → move… → up`（拖拽/滑动这类交互以前根本测不了）；
  `count{name?|controlKind?,equals|atLeast}` 回答「**建了几个**」—— 列表项、金币图标、连击星这类动态 UI 恰恰要问数量。
- **`op=frames`：按时间出多帧 + **帧间像素差** + 字段级变化**：每个时间点一张 PNG，外加 `changedPixels` / `changedRatio` /
  变化区域 `bbox` 与 **`changedControls`（哪个控件的哪个字段变了）**，回答「动画到底动没动、动的是哪一块」。
- **面板按「人一边看、AI 一边测」重排成 1:2**：右 2 份 = 试玩页（iframe，人真能在里面玩）；左 1 份 = ① 画面与日志 →
  ② 试玩操作（高级折叠）→ ③ 验收单 → ④ 工程与控件树 / **工程适配**（扫描活文件 → 勾选交接值 → 一键搭进模拟器）。
- **esbuild 打包脚本 + 产物入库**：试玩页依赖的浏览器引擎打成单个 ESM（552 KB，含 pixi）**随包发布**，
  装插件的人不用自己构建；`--check` 现打一份比字节、`prepublishOnly` 也跑一遍，防止「改了源码忘重打包 → 页面跑旧引擎且不报错」。

### 体验优化

- **画布 / 人数 / 视角固定为 PC 16:9 · 1 人 · P1**，面板与试玩页上的三个下拉**整块删掉**。两条理由：
  ① 引擎的「切设备」会**重建整个运行时**，画布一变，16:9 的舞台尺寸与 AI 记下的操作坐标都要重算；
  ② 原来那份清单是**手写**的，里面三个预设引擎里**并不存在**，选中就报 `unknown canvas preset`。
  **能力没丢**：AI 仍可用 `miliastra_sim {"op":"play","action":"device"|"view"}` 与 `playerCount` 改。
- **试玩页 footer 变成「自我诊断」**：印 `窗 · 头 · 主 · 脚 · 台` **五个高度** + 页面**版本戳**。
  以前只知道「画布很小」，现在一眼看出是**哪一层**被压（窗口 = 面板没给够高度 / 脚大 = 页面格子串位 / 主小 = 页面行没拉满）。
  版本戳还能回答「面板里那份页面是新是旧」—— 不用再靠猜有没有生效。
- **面板左列自己滚、右列不动**；最常看的放最上面，工程与控件树默认**折叠**。
- **面板左列加 300px 宽度下限**，按钮精简到 4 个核心动作，其余收进默认折叠的「试玩操作（高级）」。
- **窄容器（面板里那 ~570px）收一档**：长标题换短标题、按钮与间距收紧，工具栏努力保持一行，不再把舞台挤没。
- **README 顶部加「大字」目标声明 + 「AI 反馈区」**：目标是**让 AI 更好用**，附四条可执行尺子与三种提法；
  同一份邀请也写进了系统提示段（只有工具 schema 与提示段能自动到达 AI，只写在 README 里等于没说过）。

### 问题修复

- **★★★ 「画面咋就这么点大」的第三次根因：footer 抢走了 217px**。页面是四行网格（工具栏 / 报错条 / 主区 / 页脚），
  而报错条默认 `display:none` —— **`display:none` 的元素不生成盒子、也就不是网格项**，于是自动排行把后面三个**各上提一格**：
  主区落到 `auto` 行（行高 = 舞台高 ⇒ 又变成「自己量自己」）、**页脚落到 `1fr` 行（实测 217px）**，真正那 26px 的行没人占。
  作者截图里页脚文字下面那一大片「空白」就是它，跟画面一点关系都没有。修法：四个元素**各自显式 `grid-row`**（隐藏的那行塌成 0），
  并给报错条加 `max-height:40%` —— 报错再长也不许把舞台挤没。修后画布 **512×288**（修前 160×90）。
  ⚠️ 这个坑**读代码发现不了**（CSS 逐行看完全正确）：是对截图**按列打印像素色带**、量出页脚底色铺了 217px 才定的案。
- **★★ 舞台高度被画布「自己量自己」锁成一条缝**：`main` 只写了列、**行是 `auto`** ⇒ 行高 = 内容高 = **画布的高度**，
  而画布高度又是从舞台盒子量出来算的 ⇒ 某次算小之后一路变小、最后锁死（列宽由容器分配，所以"宽度一直正常、高度一直不对"）。
  改成把行拉满 + 舞台 `height:100%`：**舞台高度由容器决定，永远不看画布**。
- **★★ `/miliastra/engine` 把请求体里的 `op` / `action` 吃掉了（真事故：面板试玩按钮与试玩页双双**静默**失效）**。
  路由早先写成「有 `body.args` 就用 `body.args`」，而 `op=play` 的参数本来就装在 `args` 里 ⇒ `op/action` 一起被丢，
  每次调用退化成默认的 `op=state`，**全程不报错**。后果是试玩页永远接不上会话（**一片黑、Frame 停在 0**）、
  面板的「开始试玩 / 按键 / 单步 / 连帧」全部白发。现在请求体**原样**交给引擎，并用两条断言 + 一条源码绊线钉住。
- **★ 重启 `dsh web` 后工程回到「出厂默认」（看起来就像什么都没画）**：Host 是启动快照，内存里的工程会被重置。
  现在 `op=state` 直接上报 `factoryDefault`，面板顶部出现提示条 + **「一键重搭上次」**（读成功 `bind` 时记下的配方）
  —— **不自动重搭**，不擅自在人没要求时改工程。
- **★ 试玩页的报错以前看不见**：报错条原来放在默认折叠的侧栏里，于是「WebGL 起不来 / 会话没跑起来」一个字都看不到，
  用户看到的就是一片黑。现在它是常驻在工具栏下面的红条，WebGL 初始化也包了 `try/catch` 并给出下一步建议。
- **★ 面板左列的按钮 / 文字会叠在一起**：左列是固定高度的弹性列，子项默认会被压扁（`flex-shrink:1` + `min-height:0`），
  内容一超就互相重叠。现在子项一律 `flex:0 0 auto`，滚动交给容器。
- **★ 画面被挤到左下角、右侧试玩页被滚出视野**：滚动模型改成左列自己滚、右列不动。
- **引擎两处**：① `imageType` 放开为可写 —— 上游保守拒绝，但真机脚本对即时实例化的图片写它并**跑通**了，
  继续拒绝会变成**假阴性**（模拟器跑不起来、真机没问题）；② `slimPlay` 原来无条件丢掉 `scene`，
  与「`summaryOnly` 只去体积」的约定矛盾，直接后果是试玩页永远拿不到画面。

### 其他变更

- 测试 **597 项**全绿（`readme` 14 / `smoke` 53 / `deploy` 30 / `probe-deploy` 16 / `lualint` 32 / `shot` 104 /
  `sim` 132 / `sim-play` 41 / `client-render` 45 / 引擎 130）。版本号四处一致（`package.json` / `index.js` / README 两处）。
- **真机证据**：`op=bind` 在真机关卡《冰镜·火烛》上 370ms 建好，`run.logs` 里出现脚本自己 print 的
  `就绪（3 关，控件 31，画布 1600x900）`（与真机 `.gia` 同一句），`run.controlCount=32`；
  交接值三个全中，`local LIMIT = 60` 这类小整数不会被误收。
- **文档**：新增「模拟器在流程里的位置 = 真机试玩之前的**预测试**」（三档：①看 ②玩 ③判，以及②与③的区别），
  并把同一份定位写进工具 schema 与系统提示段（`smoke` 有绊线：少了它，AI 会拿模拟器结果当"验过了"汇报）。
- 两条老规矩不变：**Host 半边是启动快照**（改 `index.js` / `lib/*.mjs` 要重启 `dsh web`；只改 `lib/client.js` 刷新页面即可）；
  **面板没有的功能不代表工具没有** —— 工具 schema 才是唯一真身。
- ⚠️ **已知边界**：**模拟器通过 ≠ 真机通过**；导出的 `.gia` **能否被官方编辑器接受仍未验证**（两个方向都只能人做）；
  试玩页的画面**观感与手感**仍待人工过目（本机没有浏览器自动化，产物与数据通路有测试钉住，最后一米只能人看）；
  1–8 人是本地多客户端模拟，**不含真实联机**。

**Full Changelog**: [v0.1.0...v0.2.0](https://github.com/LoktLin/dsh-miliastra/compare/v0.1.0...v0.2.0)

---

This release follows `v0.1.0`. It **connects the simulator to the real machine** and brings the **browser playtest page**
into the repository: `op=handover` pulls handover values straight out of your script (no more copying 9-digit ids by hand),
`op=bind` sets your real project up inside the simulator in one call, `GET /miliastra/play` is a PixiJS (WebGL) page you can
**actually play** (sharing **one session** with the panel and with the AI), and `op=cases` turns "how this version gets accepted"
into a checklist humans and AI read from the same file. Three separate root causes behind "why is the viewport so small"
are fixed as well — the sneakiest one being a footer that had quietly claimed 217px.

<h3 id="en-v0.2.0">New Features</h3>

- **★ Browser playtest page `GET /miliastra/play`**: a real, playable PixiJS (WebGL) page — toolbar (start / pause / step / restart / stop)
  plus a side panel (status / server variables / script `print` / **this run's action timeline**). It shares **one session and one project**
  with the panel and the AI; the page polls scene deltas every 33 ms, so **as soon as the AI acts, the picture in front of you changes**.
  The page `attach()`es to a running session first and only starts a new run if there is none — it will not knock over a run you or the AI are using.
- **★ `op=handover`: check handover values instead of copying them by hand**: lists the live files on this machine (flagging the one
  currently under development), reads that Lua, and lays out the **candidate handover values** found in `local NAME = <9+ digit integer>`
  (with variable names and type hints) plus a suggested template list. Why it earns its own step: **one wrong digit means the script
  silently creates nothing** — no error, no trace in the log. Extracting the real value beats asking someone to retype it.
- **★ `op=bind`: bring the real project into the simulator in one call**: give it `source` (live file path) +
  `templates:[{guid,kind}]` (**the template indices handed over by the creator**) + `containerId`. It runs a session for you and reports
  whether the script ran (`run.logs`) and how many controls exist (`run.controlCount`); a successful bind **records a recipe**, so
  `{"op":"bind","last":true}` rebuilds it later.
- **★ `op=cases`: an acceptance sheet humans and AI read from the same file**: automated cases are **replayed deterministically**;
  **manual entries are only listed — never run, never judged**. The reply says plainly: "automated cases done — but the set is not accepted yet: N manual items remain".
- **`op=verify` with `fromHistory:true`: the run a human just played** becomes a regression case — the AI does not have to copy events by hand.
- **`op=verify` gains drag and count assertions**: `drag:{from,to,steps?,gap?}` expands into `down → move… → up`
  (dragging and swiping used to be untestable); `count{name?|controlKind?,equals|atLeast}` answers "**how many were created**",
  which is exactly the question for dynamic UI such as list rows, coin icons and combo stars.
- **`op=frames`: multiple frames over time + **pixel deltas between them** + field-level changes**: one PNG per time point plus
  `changedPixels` / `changedRatio` / a change-region `bbox` and **`changedControls` (which field of which control moved)** — answering
  "did the animation move at all, and which part moved".
- **The panel is rearranged 1:2 around "human watches, AI tests"**: the right 2/3 is the playtest page (an iframe you can really play in);
  the left 1/3 is ① picture and log → ② play controls (advanced, collapsed) → ③ acceptance sheet → ④ project and control tree / **project fitting**
  (scan live files → tick handover values → build it into the simulator).
- **An esbuild bundle script, with the artifact committed**: the browser engine the page needs is bundled into a single ESM (552 KB, pixi included)
  and **ships with the package**, so installers do not have to build anything. `--check` rebuilds and compares byte-for-byte, and
  `prepublishOnly` runs it too — preventing "edited the source, forgot to rebuild, page runs an old engine and reports nothing".

### Improvements

- **Canvas / player count / view are pinned to PC 16:9 · 1 player · P1**, and the three dropdowns are **gone** from the panel and the page.
  Two reasons: ① switching device **rebuilds the whole runtime**, and once the canvas changes, the 16:9 stage size and any coordinates the AI
  recorded have to be recomputed; ② the old list was **hand-written** and contained three presets the engine does not have, so selecting one
  errored with `unknown canvas preset`. **No capability is lost**: the AI can still change them via
  `miliastra_sim {"op":"play","action":"device"|"view"}` and `playerCount`.
- **The playtest page footer became self-diagnosing**: it prints **five heights** (`window · header · main · footer · stage`) plus a page
  **version stamp**. Previously you only knew "the canvas is small"; now you can see **which layer** is being squeezed
  (small window = the panel is not giving it height / large footer = the page's grid rows shifted / small main = the row is not filling).
  The stamp also answers "is the page inside my panel the new one" — no more guessing whether a change took effect.
- **The panel's left column scrolls on its own and the right one stays put**; the most-watched cards are on top and the project/control tree
  starts **collapsed**.
- **The left column has a 300px width floor**, its buttons are trimmed to 4 core actions, and the rest moved into a collapsed "play controls (advanced)".
- **Narrow containers (the ~570px inside the panel) step down a size**: shorter title, tighter buttons and gaps, so the toolbar stays on one line
  instead of squeezing the stage out.
- **The README gains a large goal statement and an "AI feedback" section**: the goal is to **make this better for AI**, with four measurable
  rules and three ways to contribute; the same invitation is repeated in the system prompt (only the tool schema and the prompt section reach
  the AI automatically — putting it in the README alone means it was never said).

### Bug Fixes

- **★★★ The third root cause of "why is the viewport so tiny": the footer had claimed 217px.** The page is a four-row grid
  (toolbar / error strip / main / footer), and the error strip is `display:none` by default — **a `display:none` element generates no box,
  so it is not a grid item**, which made auto-placement pull everything after it up one row: main landed in the `auto` row
  (row height = stage height, i.e. back to "measuring itself"), **the footer landed in the `1fr` row and measured 217px**, and the real 26px
  row was left empty. The big "blank area" under the footer text in the screenshot *was the footer itself* and had nothing to do with the viewport.
  Fix: each of the four elements now claims its row **explicitly** (the hidden row collapses to 0), and the error strip is capped at `max-height:40%`
  so even a long error cannot squeeze the stage away. The canvas went from **160×90 to 512×288**.
  ⚠️ This one **cannot be found by reading the code** (the CSS is correct line by line): it was pinned down by **printing pixel colour bands column by column**
  over the screenshot and measuring that the footer background spanned 217px.
- **★★ The stage height was "measuring itself" down to a slit**: `main` declared columns only, so **its row was `auto`** ⇒ row height = content height
  = **the canvas height**, while the canvas height was itself computed from the stage box ⇒ once it shrank, it kept shrinking until it locked
  (column widths come from the container, hence the symptom "width always fine, height always wrong"). Now the row fills and the stage is `height:100%`:
  **the stage height comes from the container and never looks at the canvas**.
- **★★ `/miliastra/engine` swallowed `op` / `action` from the request body (a real incident: the panel's play buttons and the playtest page both
  failed *silently*)**. The route used to read "if there is a `body.args`, use `body.args`" — but `op=play` carries its arguments inside `args`,
  so `op/action` were dropped together and every call degraded to the default `op=state` **with no error at all**. The result: the playtest page
  could never attach (a **black screen, stuck at Frame 0**) and the panel's start / key / step / burst buttons all did nothing. The body is now passed
  through **verbatim**, pinned by two assertions plus a source-level tripwire.
- **★ After restarting `dsh web`, the project falls back to the factory default (which looks like nothing was ever drawn)**: the Host is a startup
  snapshot, so the in-memory project resets. `op=state` now reports `factoryDefault`, and the panel shows a notice with **"rebuild the last one"**
  (reading the recipe recorded by a successful `bind`) — it **never rebuilds on its own**, we do not change your project unless asked.
- **★ Errors on the playtest page used to be invisible**: the error strip lived in the collapsed side panel, so "no WebGL" or "the session did not start"
  showed nothing at all and all you saw was black. It is now a permanent red strip under the toolbar, and WebGL initialisation is wrapped in `try/catch`
  with a concrete next step.
- **★ Buttons and text in the panel's left column overlapped**: it is a fixed-height flex column whose children shrink by default
  (`flex-shrink:1` + `min-height:0`), so overflow squashed and overlapped them. Children are now `flex:0 0 auto` and scrolling belongs to the container.
- **★ The viewport was pushed into the bottom-left corner and the playtest page scrolled out of sight**: the scroll model is now "left column scrolls, right one does not".
- **Two engine fixes**: ① `imageType` is now writable — upstream conservatively rejected it, but a real script writes it for instantly instantiated images
  and it works on device, so rejecting it became a **false negative** (the simulator fails while the real thing is fine); ② `slimPlay` unconditionally
  dropped `scene`, contradicting "`summaryOnly` only removes bytes", and the direct consequence was that the playtest page could never receive a picture.

### Chores

- **597 checks** pass (`readme` 14 / `smoke` 53 / `deploy` 30 / `probe-deploy` 16 / `lualint` 32 / `shot` 104 /
  `sim` 132 / `sim-play` 41 / `client-render` 45 / engine 130). The version is consistent in all four places
  (`package.json` / `index.js` / two spots in the README).
- **On-device evidence**: `op=bind` built the real level "冰镜·火烛" in 370 ms; `run.logs` contains the script's own
  `就绪（3 关，控件 31，画布 1600x900）` (the same line that appears in the on-device `.gia`), and `run.controlCount=32`.
  All three handover values were found, and small integers such as `local LIMIT = 60` are not mis-collected.
- **Docs**: a new section placing the simulator in the pipeline as the **pre-test before playing on device** (three tiers: ① look ② play ③ judge,
  and how ② differs from ③), with the same positioning written into the tool schema and the system prompt (a `smoke` tripwire guards it: without it,
  the AI reports simulator results as "verified").
- Two long-standing rules are unchanged: **the Host half is a startup snapshot** (restart `dsh web` after changing `index.js` / `lib/*.mjs`;
  changing only `lib/client.js` needs a page refresh) and **a feature missing from the panel does not mean the tool lacks it** — the tool schema is the source of truth.
- ⚠️ **Known limits**: **passing in the simulator ≠ passing on device**; whether an exported `.gia` is **accepted by the official editor is still unverified**
  (both directions need a human); the playtest page's **look and feel** still needs a human eye (there is no browser automation here — the artifact and the data
  path are covered by tests, but the last metre is human); and 1–8 players is a local multi-client simulation, **not real networking**.

**Full Changelog**: [v0.1.0...v0.2.0](https://github.com/LoktLin/dsh-miliastra/compare/v0.1.0...v0.2.0)
